chunks: 1- Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd, from Nashit ibn Salih, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: How much water suffices in istinja' from urine? He said: The like of what is on the glans of moisture.

2- As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd, from Nashit, from some of our companions, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
For urine, it suffices that you wash it with the like of it.

So it does not contradict the first report, because his statement, “It suffices that you wash it with the like of it,” may be understood as referring back to the urine itself, not to what remained; and that is more than what we considered of twice the amount of what is upon it.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءِ: cleansing the private part after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْبَلَلِ: moisture or wetness remaining on the organ
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, the impurity being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْحَشَفَةِ: the glans, used here as a measure for remaining moisture
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the first report, cited for reconciliation with the later narration
key_terms.تَغْسِلَهُ: to wash it, meaning to cleanse the affected area
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient; fulfills the required minimum

ai.seo_question: How much water suffices for istinja' from urine according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the amount of water sufficient for istinja' from urine and presents two narrations on the measure. The closing explanation reconciles them by interpreting the second report as referring to the amount of urine itself, making it consistent with the first and supporting a fiqh ruling on ritual purity.
